Engineering

Implementation test and review standard

Assertions target ownership, transactions and actual consumers—not only isolated asset creation.

On this page
Test layersMinimum change reviewRegression orderEvidence formatting

Test layers

Static documentation tests detect link/manifest/order/coverage problems. Editor data validation detects bad definitions/IDs/references. Native unit tests check pure math and state transitions. Backend integration tests use real transactions and competing connections. Functional tests run packaged/Editor clients and dedicated servers. None substitutes for all the others.

Minimum change review

  1. Check the owner and stable IDs match manifest and ownership records.
  2. Inspect native Blueprint exposure and replication conditions for private facts.
  3. Run success, invalid input, stale revision, duplicate command with same/different payload, concurrent claim and disconnect-after-commit.
  4. Test missing definition/animation and world teardown to prove presentation is not a gameplay gate.
  5. Reopen actual consuming Blueprint, data asset and map; confirm the assignment exists and is used.
  6. Record build/tool versions, commands, fixtures and observed results. Leave not_run where no runtime exists.

Regression order

Start with terrain/one-pawn/input foundation; then identity/persistence/handoff; then GAS/enemy/reward; inventory/economy; professions/quest; skills/world/social; operations/release. A new guild widget cannot justify ignoring a broken inventory transaction or duplicate possession.

Evidence formatting

A test report needs TestCaseId, build/catalog/schema versions, platform/hardware/network conditions, setup, command, expected, observed, result and evidence paths. Screenshots alone rarely prove economic invariants; inspect database rows/receipt IDs too. Never generate fictional compiler or test logs.

Planned game assets are not compiled assets. Values are proposals unless explicitly evidenced. Verification and limitations.
